text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The attorney-general is criticised by Kenyan opposition leaders for starting work on a constitutional review commission bill without consulting them.
- Police round up at least 80 suspected perpetrators of the Rwandan genocide in Kenya.
- Former powerful cabinet minister Kipkalya Kones who was dropped in a cabinet reshuffle in January is pardoned by President Daniel arap Moi and welcomed back to the ruling party's fold.
- John Ward, father of the British tourist girl believed to have been murdered nine years ago, says he has found his daughter's killers.
- Moi lashes out at the head of the National Council of Churches of Kenya for attempting to teach him politics.
- Kenya's Daniel Komen sets a new world record for the 3000 metres -- 7:58.61 at the International Athletics Meeting in Belgium.
- The Anglican Church in Kenya declares its support for the government's initiative to have dialogue with the opposition.
- A nine-year old girl is said to have stolen a two-month month old baby boy.
- President Moi and opposiiton leader Michael Kijana Wamalwa share a platform -- a show of solidarity to their commitment to peaceful talks on constitutional reforms.
- The sudden decision by the Kenyan government to move on constitutional reforms followed a period of unprecedented international pressure sparked by political unrest on July 7.
- Kenyan police gave Rwanda and Uganda a major intelligence victory when they arrested Colonel Gratien Kabiligi, former head of the presidential guard in Kigali.
- Tanzania orders its defence organs in Kigoma at the Burundi Tanzania border to investigate the killings of three Tanzanians allegedly by members of the Burundi army. ($1=59 Kenyan Shillings)
